sections.title: Before reading: study Chapter 7 in How to read. Two coverings match; pointing is misunderstood

segments.text: 門閉，人在門內。寧持卷，客持書。人持燈，視卷。客指書，安視書，問。
客開帙，開書。寧視書，客持紙。紙有姓，紙乾。書有破葉。安視姓，寧視半字。人呼安，安應。
人持燈，安取燈。安持燈，視卷。寧還卷，人取卷。卷有帙，人視卷，閉帙。寧視帙。人指卷，安視帙。
客閉書，書有帙。客閉帙，持書。
客持書，人取書。人假書，持兩束，客持紙。帙同，書異。
安立，視兩束。此束在左，彼束在右。寧視紙，客持紙。
客不答，持紙。人指此束，安視此束。寧視客，不視此束。
人呼寧，寧應。寧視彼束，不別兩束。寧指彼束。
寧取書，持書。人持卷，視寧。安持燈，寧視帙。

sections.title: The corrected bundle reveals a different problem

segments.text: 客開帙，開書。客視破葉。書乾。客持紙，安視紙。帙乾。客視紙，紙無水。客閉書，閉帙。寧先視印，視帙。寧持卷，安持燈。燈明，火明。人視此束，寧識印。寧視彼束，客持書。
寧持卷，帙有水。寧視帙，止。
寧呼人，人應。安持燈，至寧。寧還卷，人取卷。人持此束，寧視印。人開帙，開卷。人讀卷，止。卷有全葉，葉有字。人視葉，寧視卷。
客持書，持紙。安指印，寧視此束。寧不取卷，人持卷。安視帙，客視卷。
人呼安，安應。安持燈至人，人視葉。寧視卷，客持紙。
人不閉卷，持此束。人不還卷，寧待人。寧不出門，安持燈。客持彼束，門閉。

grammar.title: 此束有卷，彼束有書。
grammar.rule: 此｜束；彼｜束；是｜束。此束有卷，彼束有書。
grammar.note_en:
Study Chapter7 in How to read before the story. Read the cards in dependency order, then attempt the four retrieval packets and reference contrasts. They preserve all24 packet attempts; eleven extra earlier-role/question retrievals supplement the full workbook and Pensa. Traditional characters and Mandarin citation readings remain the display convention, not reconstructed ancient sound.

A demonstrative points to a selected object. 此 cǐ before a noun means this, and 彼 bǐ means that. 此束有卷 means “This bundle contains the fascicle”; 彼束有書 means “That bundle contains the book.” The reader’s pointing identifies the first while Ning attends to the second. Her 此束有卷, “This bundle contains the fascicle,” is a mistaken claim about the object she herself points to. Attributed speech is not narrator-certified truth. Her attention and the similar covers explain the wrong selection; she does not acquire an owner’s identity from either cover.

是 shì before a noun has the selected demonstrative meaning this: 是束有卷 means “This bundle contains the fascicle,” and 寧假是束 means “Ning borrows this bundle.” It is not the modern linking verb is and does not replace 也. The reader’s 誰假是束？ “Who will borrow this bundle?” is the familiar prospective offer; Ning’s answer and the explicit handoff establish the corrected loan. She had borrowed this reader’s separate fascicle in chapter6, returned it for comparison, and taken the wrong covered book. The wrong taking is not certified as a separate authorised loan.

Pointing follows each speaker. 寧指卷。寧：「此束有印。」 means “Ning points to the fascicle: This bundle has a mark.” 客指書。客：「此束無印。」 means “The guest points to the book: This bundle has no mark.” The same 此 can select different objects because the pointing and speakers change. It does not permanently name a book or a left-hand item. The narrative’s side labels remain from An’s fixed viewing position: 此束在左，彼束在右, “This bundle is on the left, that one on the right.” Later 寧在左，客在右, “Ning is on the left, the guest on the right,” tracks the holders. No new compound left hand/right hand is assumed.

束 shù is a bundle noun, not a binding verb. 卷有帙, “The fascicle has a wrapper,” names this particular wrapped object as a 束; it does not equate every scroll with a bundle. The messenger’s book also has a wrapper, without proving it is the book’s original case. 兩 liǎng means two; 兩束 liǎng shù counts the selected two bundles, without requiring things counted by 兩 to form a natural pair. Only this finite count is practised here; general numeral and unit patterns come later. 帙同，書異 means “The covers match, the books differ”: outward covering can match without identical contents, a single shared case or matching works.

印 yìn is a mark or seal impression on the wrapper. It is not the act of stamping and supplies no unprinted name. One case has it and the other lacks it; that difference identifies which object was lent. 別 bié means distinguish the pair: 安別兩束 “An distinguishes the two bundles,” followed by 寧…別兩束 “Ning distinguishes them.” It is not leave or an adjective other. 識印 means recognising this particular mark, continuing the earlier identifying-mark sense of 識 rather than broad literacy. 主 remains the ultimate book owner, still unknown. The guest’s 客不知主 “The guest does not know the owner” is attributed speech, not verification of his commission.

先 xiān means first or earlier. Here it is practised only before the inspection verb 視, in 安先視卷 “An first looks at the fascicle,” 人先視印 “The person first looks at the mark,” and 寧先視印 “Ning first looks at the mark.” Its position selects the first inspection. The earlier 先生 xiānshēng is one teacher title, not automatic teaching of standalone 先. 誤 wù stays a noun: 寧有誤 “Ning has made a mistake,” 安…知誤 “An knows the error,” 寧知誤 “Ning recognises the error.” No new verb meaning impede, miss or mislead is being practised.

乾 gān is dry, 濕 shī wet. 書乾，紙乾 and 帙乾 state that the messenger’s book, sheet and wrapper are dry. They do not claim a drying action or identify a water source. 寧：「此帙濕。」 “This wrapper is wet,” follows 帙有水 “The wrapper has water on it.” 人：「卷濕。」 “The fascicle is wet,” and 安：「是束濕。」 “This bundle is wet,” extend the discovery from wrapper to contained material and the identified package. Predicates need no added verb be. Not dry and wet are not universal synonyms; retain the stated quality. The reader stops reading and keeps the wet fascicle for inspection. Nothing has instantly dried.

All remain inside the closed near gate. An receives the lamp on a new explicit loan before the reader handles both wrapped objects. The reader temporarily borrows the messenger’s large book. After the mistaken taking, Ning returns that book to the reader, who returns it to the messenger. A corrected explicit offer restores the marked fascicle to Ning; she later returns it for wetness inspection. At the end An has the lamp, the reader the wet marked fascicle and wrapper, and the messenger the dry large book, case and separate surname sheet. Parents, teacher, old loose leaves, mother’s small book and original An sheet remain far home. Neither the case mark nor a held surname sheet proves ownership.
